sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: BROAD WRN ONT UPR LOW WILL MOVE SLOWLY E THROUGH THE PERIOD... WHILE FLAT RIDGE PERSISTS OVER THE SRN PLNS. SEASONABLY STRONG SHORTWAVE TROUGH ON SRN SIDE OF THE LOW...NOW APPROACHING LK ONT...WILL CONTINUE ENE INTO SRN QUE LATER TODAY...WHILE THE SRN PART OF THE TROUGH GRAZES ERN NY AND WRN/NRN NEW ENGLAND. IN THE WEST...LEAD PORTION OF SLOWLY PROGRESSIVE NV UPR VORT IS NOW OVER UT. THIS FEATURE WILL CONTINUE E INTO CO THIS AFTN...AND ACROSS THE CNTRL HI PLNS TONIGHT. OVER THE NRN GULF...REMNANT OF TROPICAL DEPRESSION FIVE EXPECTED TO DRIFT SLOWLY W THROUGH THE PERIOD. AT LWR LEVELS...COLD FRONT ATTENDANT TO ONT TROUGH WILL MOVE STEADILY E ACROSS NY/NEW ENGLAND...AND MORE SLOWLY SE ACROSS THE MID ATLANTIC REGION /WHERE IT WILL BE PRECEDED BY A LEE TROUGH/. FARTHER W...LEE TROUGH WILL STRENGTHEN OVER THE CNTRL HI PLNS...AHEAD OF UPR IMPULSE APPROACHING FROM THE GRT BASIN.

sections.title: ERN NY/NEW ENGLAND/MID ATLANTIC THIS AFTN AND EARLY EVE
sections.text: WEAK HEIGHT FALLS WILL OVERSPREAD THE LWR GRT LKS AND WRN/NRN NEW ENGLAND TODAY AS ONT SHORTWAVE TROUGH EJECTS NE ACROSS ONT/QUE. ALTHOUGH STRONGEST FORCING FOR ASCENT WILL REMAIN N OF REGION... COMBINATION OF INCREASING ASCENT...MODEST SFC HEATING...AND LOW LVL MOISTURE TRANSPORT/WAA LIKELY WILL SUPPORT A CONTINUED INCREASE OF STORM COVERAGE/INTENSITY ALONG/AHEAD OF ASSOCIATED COLD FRONT /REF WW 618/. OTHER STORMS MAY FORM A BIT LATER TODAY SWWD INTO ERN PA...MD...AND VA...IN ZONE OF GREATER HEATING/CONVERGENCE ALONG LEE TROUGH. SEASONABLY STRONG /40+ KT/ UNIDIRECTIONAL WSWLY MID-UPR LVL FLOW WILL CONTINUE TO SUPPORT SUSTAINED STORMS...WITH ORGANIZATION INTO SHORT LINE SEGMENTS/BANDS...AND PERHAPS A FEW SUPERCELLS. THESE STORMS WILL BE CAPABLE OF DMGG SFC WINDS AND SVR HAIL. A CONDITIONAL TORNADO THREAT ALSO COULD EVOLVE...MAINLY IN FAR ERN NY AND WRN/CNTRL NEW ENGLAND. ANY SUSTAINED STORMS MOVING INTO THAT REGION WILL ENCOUNTER SFC WINDS THAT WILL REMAIN SOMEWHAT BACKED BENEATH COMPARATIVELY STRONG 850 FLOW. THE MORNING SATELLITE IMAGERY SUGGESTS THAT SOMEWHAT GREATER LOW LVL INSTABILITY/LAPSE RATES SHOULD DEVELOP OVER PARTS OF PA...NJ...MD...DE...AND VA...WHERE SBCAPE COULD REAC

sections.title: CNTRL HI PLNS LATE THIS AFTN/TONIGHT
sections.text: LEAD PORTION OF GRT BASIN UPR VORT SHOULD REACH ERN UT/SW WY BY 00Z. THIS SHOULD ENHANCE LARGE SCALE ASCENT OVER THE CNTRL RCKYS AND ADJACENT HI PLNS LATER TODAY...AND STRENGTHEN ASSOCIATED SSELY LOW LVL UPSLOPE FLOW/LEE TROUGH. SCTD SHOWERS AND...BY AFTN...A FEW TSTMS MAY OCCUR OVER THE CNTRL HI PLNS TODAY. BUT STRONGER/SVR STORMS ARE EXPECTED LATER TODAY INTO TONIGHT AS STORMS/ASCENT ASSOCIATED WITH UPR IMPULSE MOVE/DEVELOP E OFF THE HIGHER TERRAIN. ALTHOUGH CLOUDS WILL SOMEWHAT LIMIT/DELAY DIURNAL HEATING OVER THE HI PLNS...AMPLE INSTABILITY /SBCAPE OF 1000-1500 J PER KG/ SHOULD DEVELOP TO SUPPORT STRONG UPDRAFTS. BAND OF 25-30 KT WLY MID LVL WINDS SKIRTING SRN SIDE OF SHORTWAVE IMPULSE...COUPLED WITH 15-20 KT SSELY NEAR-SFC FLOW...SHOULD FOSTER SCTD SUSTAINED STORMS/SUPERCELLS. THESE WILL POSE A RISK FOR LARGE HAIL... LOCALLY DMGG WIND...AND PERHAPS A TORNADO...INTO TONIGHT. THE STORMS SHOULD MOVE/DEVELOP E INTO CNTRL NEB/KS AS AN MCS OR TWO LATER TONIGHT/EARLY TUE AS LLJ STRENGTHENS AND VEERS WITH CONTINUED EWD MOVEMENT OF UPR IMPULSE. WEAKER INSTABILITY AND NOCTURNAL COOLING SHOULD LIMIT ANY LATE NIGHT SVR THREAT.

sections.title: ELSEWHERE
sections.text: VERY WARM SFC TEMPERATURES AND STEEP LOW LVL LAPSE RATES WILL CONTRIBUTE TO SCTD DIURNALLY ENHANCED STORMS OVER NW TX AND NM. OTHER STRONG STORMS/STORM CLUSTERS MAY EVOLVE WITHIN BELT OF ENHANCED LWR TROPOSPHERIC FLOW ON NRN FRINGE OF CIRCULATION IN THE NRN GULF...NEWD INTO THE SRN APPALACHIANS. HIGH PW VALUES AND STRONG HEATING MAY YIELD LOCALLY STRONG MICROBURSTS. ..CORFIDI/HURLBUT.. 08/16/2010

sections.title: THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS OVER THE CNTRL HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: ...NEW ENGLAND INTO THE MID ATLANTIC STATES... MORNING WATER VAPOR IMAGERY INDICATES A SIGNIFICANT SHORT WAVE TROUGH ROTATING NEWD THROUGH THE LOWER GREAT LAKES...WHICH SHOULD CONTINUE INTO QUEBEC TODAY. THIS SYSTEM IS ATTENDED BY A 50-70 KT MIDLEVEL JET STREAK WHICH WILL CONCURRENTLY PROPAGATE NEWD ACROSS THE NRN HALF OF NEW ENGLAND. AT THE SURFACE...AN ASSOCIATED COLD FRONT WILL PROGRESS EWD...LIKELY EXTENDING FROM THE CHAMPLAIN VALLEY SWWD INTO THE BLUE RIDGE BY LATE AFTERNOON. THIS FRONT WILL SERVE AS THE FOCUS FOR STRONG TO SEVERE TSTM DEVELOPMENT TODAY. A BAND OF TSTMS ARE DEVELOPING ALONG THE COLD FRONT AS OF MID/LATE MORNING OVER PORTIONS OF UPSTATE NY INTO CNTRL PA...LIKELY DRIVEN BY A COMBINATION OF ASCENT ALONG THE FRONT AND DEEPER FORCING ATTENDANT TO ABOVE-MENTIONED SHORT WAVE TROUGH. WIDESPREAD CLOUDINESS SHOULD TEND TO DIMINISH BY AFTERNOON...ALLOWING FOR AREAS OF STRONGER HEATING. WHEN COUPLED WITH THE MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER /I.E. DEW POINTS IN THE 70S/ AIR MASS WILL BECOME MODERATELY UNSTABLE BY AFTERNOON WITH MLCAPE VALUES APPROACHING 1000-1500 J/KG OVER NRN NEW ENGLAND...TO AS HIGH AS 2000-2500 J/KG FROM THE LOWER HUDSON VALLEY INTO THE VA PIEDMONT. sections.title: CNTRL HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: FORECAST TODAY IS SOMEWHAT COMPLICATED DUE TO FAIRLY WIDESPREAD CLOUDS AND THE EARLY DEVELOPMENT TSTMS OVER PORTIONS OF THE AREA. NONETHELESS...THE PRESENCE OF STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES /REF. 12Z DNR SOUNDING/...COUPLED WITH A MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER AND POCKETS OF STRONG DIABATIC HEATING ARE EXPECTED TO YIELD A MODERATELY UNSTABLE AIR MASS BY AFTERNOON WITH MLCAPE INCREASING TO 1000-2500 J/KG. THE EWD PROGRESSION OF WELL-DEFINED VORTICITY MAXIMUM FROM THE GREAT BASIN AND WEAKER...EMBEDDED DOWNSTREAM IMPULSES WILL PROVIDE SUFFICIENT BACKGROUND FORCING TO SUPPORT AN INCREASE IN STORM COVERAGE AND INTENSITY TODAY ALONG W-E ORIENTED BOUNDARY FROM CNTRL WY TO ALONG THE SD/NEB BORDER...AND INVOF MORE N-S ORIENTED FRONT/TROUGH OVER THE CO FRONT RANGE. THE STRONGEST DEEP WLY SHEAR /I.E. 40-45 KT WILL REMAIN GENERALLY TO THE N OF THE I-80 CORRIDOR...DIMINISHING TO 30-35 KT SWD THROUGH ERN CO/WRN KS. AS SUCH...GIVEN SETUP WILL BE SUPPORTIVE OF ORGANIZED STORM MODES...INCLUDING SUPERCELLS WITH A RISK FOR HAIL...LOCALLY STRONG WIND GUSTS AND PERHAPS A TORNADO. STRENGTHENING NOCTURNAL LLJ MAY SUPPORT AN UPSCALE GROWTH OF STORMS INTO AN MCS WITH A WIND AND HAIL THREAT DEVELOPING EWD ACROSS THE ER

sections.title: NEW ENGLAND INTO MID ATLANTIC STATES
sections.text: FORECAST IN THE EASTERN UNITED STATES APPEARS ON TRACK THIS AFTERNOON WITH ONLY MINOR CHANGES MADE. ISOLATED INTENSE THUNDERSTORMS WILL CONTINUE TO DEVELOP IN AXIS OF MOIST/UNSTABLE AIR FROM SOUTHERN NEW ENGLAND INTO MID ATLANTIC STATES. FARTHER NORTH...CONVECTION HAS NOT BEEN AS ACTIVE AS ANTICIPATED. HOWEVER...POTENTIAL REMAINS FOR ISOLATED SEVERE STORM DEVELOPMENT WITH DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL THROUGH THE EARLY EVENING OVER NH/VT/ME.

sections.title: CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: STORMS HAVE BEGUN TO DEVELOP OVER THE FOOTHILLS OF CENTRAL CO...AND ARE EXPECTED TO SPREAD EASTWARD THROUGH THE DAY. SUFFICIENT VERTICAL SHEAR AND STEEP LAPSE RATES WILL PROMOTE DAMAGING WIND AND HAIL THREAT IN STRONGER STORMS THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING. HAVE EXTENDED THE SLIGHT RISK AREA ACROSS MUCH OF NEB. AN ISOLATED SEVERE STORM HAS RECENTLY AFFECTED THE ONL REGION WITH DAMAGING WINDS. OTHER ISOLATED BUT INTENSE STORMS WILL BE POSSIBLE ACROSS CENTRAL NEB IN REGION OF STRONG EFFECTIVE SHEAR AND SUFFICIENT INSTABILITY. ..HART.. 08/16/2010 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1124 AM CDT MON AUG 16 2010/
